chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Nawfali, from the descendants of Nawfal ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Isa ibn Abdillah al-Umari, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said:
Regarding the illness that befalls a child, he said: 'It is an expiation for his parents.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of a child's illness in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual benefit of a child's illness, describing it as an expiation (kaffarah) for the sins of the parents. This highlights the concept of *sabr* (patience) and divine mercy, where the suffering of the innocent child serves as a means of purification for the family's spiritual accounts. The ruling underscores the interconnectedness of familial sins and rewards in Shia jurisprudence.
